title: An implantable helmet for studying repeat TBI
author: Ondek, Lucero, et al.

steps.title: Create skull phantom
steps.instruction: Euthanize a P31 male Sprague‑Dawley rat with Euthasol (100 mg/kg) followed by rapid decapitation; remove soft tissue, soak skull bones in cold water with dish detergent, then disinfect in a 1:1 solution of 30 % H₂O₂ and water; measure skull dimensions and import them into Autodesk Inventor Pro to generate a phantom for implant design.

steps.title: Design and fabricate implant
steps.instruction: Using the phantom measurements, design a 3‑D‑printed cap in Autodesk Inventor Pro that includes 0.175 mm radius half‑circles spaced 0.51 mm along the ventral face; print the implant on an Objet Connex 260v (Stratasys) with VeroWhitePlus material and adhere a 0.5 mm layer of TangoBlackPlus on top for video tracking; main body dimensions 13.0 mm L × 13.0 mm W × 4.610 mm H, wings 2.005 mm L × 13.0 mm W × 1.052 mm H; include a 10.5 mm ventral cutout for a stainless‑steel disc (10 mm diameter × 3 mm height) and a dorsal aperture of 9.3 mm (rim 0.6 mm wide × 0.5 mm thick).

steps.title: Cold‑sterilize implant caps
steps.instruction: Immerse each printed cap in a cold‑sterilization solution consisting of 33 mL Cetylcide‑G plus Cetylcide‑G Diluent (Cetylite) diluted in 946 mL sterile, deionized water for a minimum of 12 h; rinse caps three times for 1 min each with sterile deionized water; caps are single‑use and discarded after implantation.

steps.title: Pre‑operative analgesia
steps.instruction: Inject carprofen subcutaneously at 5 mg/kg 30 min before anesthesia induction.

steps.title: Induce and maintain anesthesia
steps.instruction: Place the rat in an induction chamber and deliver 4 % isoflurane in air for exactly 3 min; then maintain anesthesia with 1.5–3 % isoflurane in a 2 NO₂:1 O₂ gas mixture via nose cone; keep the animal on a heating pad set to 37.0 ± 1.5 °C.

steps.title: Prepare surgical site
steps.instruction: Shave the head, sterilize the skin by alternating alcohol and betadine wipes three times each, and inject 0.1 mL of 0.25 % bupivacaine subcutaneously directly over the planned incision.

steps.title: Expose skull and etch surface
steps.instruction: Make a midline scalp incision, retract the skin to expose the dorsal cranial surface; apply 35 % phosphoric acid dental etchant for 60 s, rinse thoroughly with sterile saline, dry first with sterile gauze then with air.

steps.title: Place anchor screw and metal disc
steps.instruction: Embed a #0‑80 stainless‑steel screw into the skull over the cerebellum; apply several drops of super‑glue gel to the ridged side of the stainless‑steel disc and affix the disc centered halfway between bregma and lambda.

steps.title: Attach implant and secure with cement
steps.instruction: Apply super‑glue gel to the bottom of the printed implant and place it directly over the disc; add a thin layer of C&B‑Metabond Adhesive Luting Cement (Parkell, Inc.) followed by a thick layer of acrylic to create a rigid seal; no sutures are required.

steps.title: Post‑operative analgesia schedule
steps.instruction: Administer carprofen subcutaneously at 5 mg/kg at 24 h and 48 h after implantation; apply 0.25 % bupivacaine around the implant at 2–5 h and again at 24 h post‑surgery.

steps.title: Injury induction day 1 (P35)
steps.instruction: Anesthetize the rat for exactly 3 min with 4 % isoflurane in a chamber, then 2 min with 2 % isoflurane via nose cone; position the animal on a stiff Styrofoam pad under the eCCI‑6.3 CCI device, lower the 5 mm stainless‑steel impactor tip and zero it with the implanted disc; terminate isoflurane 30 s before impact; for rats in the Repeat‑Injury group, deliver a single impact programmed to 5 m/s velocity and 5 mm depth past zero; for Sham and Single‑Injury groups, keep the CCI device untriggered; record the actual velocity and depth reported by the controller; keep the animal on a heating pad on the Styrofoam pad after the procedure.

steps.title: Injury induction day 2 (P38)
steps.instruction: Repeat the anesthesia, positioning, and impact protocol exactly as on P35; only rats assigned to the Repeat‑Injury group receive the 5 m/s, 5 mm impact; Sham and Single‑Injury groups receive anesthesia only.

steps.title: Injury induction day 3 (P41)
steps.instruction: Repeat the anesthesia, positioning, and impact protocol; both Repeat‑Injury and Single‑Injury groups receive the 5 m/s, 5 mm impact, while Sham rats receive anesthesia only; maintain heating pad throughout.

steps.title: Assess immediate neurological response
steps.instruction: Immediately after each impact (or 30 s after isoflurane termination for sham), evaluate the toe‑pinch reflex every 5 s and record latency until response; continuously monitor the righting reflex and record total time to return to sternal recumbency.

steps.title: Record post‑injury weight change
steps.instruction: Weigh each animal on the day of injury and again on the following days (P36 after P35 injury and P42 after P41 injury); calculate percent weight change relative to the injury day weight and record the values.
